verses.zh: 希西家王听见就撕裂衣服，披上麻布，进了耶和华的殿，
verses.en: When King Hezekiah heard this,[NOTE:1] he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went to the Lord’s temple.
notes: The verb that introduces this verse serves as a discourse particle and is untranslated; see note on “in the future” in 2:2.

verses.zh: 使家宰以利亚敬和书记舍伯那，并祭司中的长老，都披上麻布，去见亚摩斯的儿子先知以赛亚，
verses.en: Eliakim the palace supervisor, Shebna the scribe, and the leading priests,[NOTE:1] clothed in sackcloth, sent this message to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz:
notes: Heb “elders of the priests” (so KJV, NAB, NASB); NCV “the older priests”; NRSV, TEV, CEV “the senior priests.”

verses.zh: 对他说：「希西家如此说：『今日是急难、责罚、凌辱的日子，就如妇人将要生产婴孩，却没有力量生产。
verses.en: “This is what Hezekiah says:[NOTE:1] ‘This is a day of distress, insults,[NOTE:2] and humiliation,[NOTE:3] as when a baby is ready to leave the birth canal but the mother lacks the strength to push it through.[NOTE:4]
notes: In the Hebrew text this verse begins with “they said to him” (cf. NRSV).
Or “rebuke” (KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV), or “correction.”
Or “contempt”; NAB, NIV, NRSV “disgrace.”
Heb “when sons come to the cervical opening and there is no strength to give birth.”

verses.zh: 或者耶和华―你的　神听见拉伯沙基的话，就是他主人亚述王打发他来辱骂永生　神的话；耶和华―你的　神听见这话就发斥责。故此，求你为余剩的民扬声祷告。』」
verses.en: Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all these things the chief adviser has spoken on behalf of his master, the king of Assyria, who sent him to taunt the living God.[NOTE:1] When the Lord your God hears, perhaps he will punish him for the things he has said.[NOTE:2] So pray for this remnant that remains.’”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “all the words of the chief adviser whom his master, the king of Assyria, sent to taunt the living God.”
Heb “and rebuke the words which the Lord your God hears.”
Heb “and lift up a prayer on behalf of the remnant that is found.”

verses.zh: 希西家王的臣仆就去见以赛亚。
verses.en: When King Hezekiah’s servants came to Isaiah,

verses.zh: 以赛亚对他们说：「要这样对你们的主人说，耶和华如此说：『你听见亚述王的仆人亵渎我的话，不要惧怕。
verses.en: Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master this: ‘This is what the Lord has said: “Don’t be afraid because of the things you have heard—these insults the king of Assyria’s servants have hurled against me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “by which the servants of the king of Assyria have insulted me.”

verses.zh: 我必惊动（原文是使灵进入）他的心；他要听见风声就归回本地，我必使他在那里倒在刀下。』」
verses.en: Look, I will take control of his mind;[NOTE:1] he will receive a report and return to his own land. I will cut him down[NOTE:2] with a sword in his own land.”’”
notes: Heb “I will put in him a spirit.” The precise sense of רוּחַ (ruakh, “spirit”) is uncertain in this context. It may refer to a spiritual being who will take control of his mind (see 1 Kgs 22:19), or it could refer to a disposition of concern and fear. In either case the Lord’s sovereignty over the king is apparent.
Heb “cause him to fall” (so KJV, ASV, NAB), that is, “kill him.”

verses.zh: 拉伯沙基回去，正遇见亚述王攻打立拿；原来他早听见亚述王拔营离开拉吉。
verses.en: When the chief adviser heard the king of Assyria had departed from Lachish, he left and went to Libnah, where the king was campaigning.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the chief adviser returned and he found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he heard that he had departed from Lachish.”

verses.zh: 亚述王听见人论古实王特哈加说：「他出来要与你争战。」亚述王一听见，就打发使者去见希西家，吩咐他们说：
verses.en: The king[NOTE:1] heard that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia[NOTE:2] was marching out to fight him.[NOTE:3] He again sent[NOTE:4] messengers to Hezekiah, ordering them:
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Cush” (so NASB, NIV11); NIV84, NCV “the Cushite king of Egypt.”
Heb “heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, ‘He has come out to fight with you.’”
The Hebrew text has, “and he heard and he sent,” but the parallel in 2 Kgs 19:9 has וַיָּשָׁב וַיִּשְׁלַח (vayyashav vayyishlakh, “and he returned and he sent”), i.e., “he again sent.”

verses.zh: 「你们对犹大王希西家如此说：『不要听你所倚靠的　神欺哄你说：耶路撒冷必不交在亚述王的手中。
verses.en: “Tell King Hezekiah of Judah this: ‘Don’t let your God in whom you trust mislead you when he says, “Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.”

verses.zh: 你总听说亚述诸王向列国所行的乃是尽行灭绝，难道你还能得救吗？
verses.en: Certainly you have heard how the kings of Assyria have annihilated all lands.[NOTE:1] Do you really think you will be rescued?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, annihilating them.”
Heb “and will you be rescued?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “No, of course not!”

verses.zh: 我列祖所毁灭的，就是歌散、哈兰、利色，和属提・拉撒的伊甸人；这些国的神何曾拯救这些国呢？
verses.en: Were the nations whom my predecessors[NOTE:1] destroyed—the nations of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar—rescued by their gods?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fathers” (so KJV, NAB, NASB); NIV84 “forefathers”; NIV11 “predecessors”; NCV “ancestors.”
Heb “Did the gods of the nations whom my fathers destroyed rescue them—Gozan and Haran, and Rezeph and the sons of Eden who are in Telassar?”

verses.zh: 哈马的王，亚珥拔的王，西法瓦音城的王，希拿和以瓦的王，都在哪里呢？』」
verses.en: Where is the king of Hamath or the king of Arpad or the kings of Lair,[NOTE:1] Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’”
notes: Lair was a city located in northeastern Babylon. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 235.

verses.zh: 希西家从使者手里接过书信来，看完了，就上耶和华的殿，将书信在耶和华面前展开。
verses.en: Hezekiah took the letter[NOTE:1] from the messengers and read it.[NOTE:2] Then Hezekiah went up to the Lord’s temple and spread it out before the Lord.
notes: The Hebrew text has the plural, “letters.” The final mem (ם) may be dittographic (note the initial mem on the form that immediately follows). Some Greek and Aramaic witnesses have the singular. If so, one still has to deal with the yod that is part of the plural ending. J. N. Oswalt refers to various commentators who have suggested ways to understand the plural form (Isaiah [NICOT], 1:652).
In the parallel text in 2 Kgs 19:14 the verb has the plural suffix, “them,” but this may reflect a later harmonization to the preceding textual reading of “letters.”

verses.zh: 希西家向耶和华祷告说：
verses.en: Hezekiah prayed before the Lord:

verses.zh: 「坐在二基路伯上万军之耶和华―以色列的　神啊，你―惟有你是天下万国的　神，你曾创造天地。
verses.en: “O Lord of Heaven’s Armies, O God of Israel, who is enthroned on the cherubim![NOTE:1] You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the sky[NOTE:2] and the earth.
notes: The cherubim (singular “cherub”) refer to the images of winged angelic creatures that were above the ark of the covenant.
Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你侧耳而听；耶和华啊，求你睁眼而看，要听西拿基立的一切话，他是打发使者来辱骂永生　神的。
verses.en: Pay attention, Lord, and hear! Open your eyes, Lord, and observe! Listen to this entire message Sennacherib sent and how he taunts the living God![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Hear all the words of Sennacherib which he sent to taunt the living God.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，亚述诸王果然使列国和列国之地变为荒凉，
verses.en: It is true, Lord, that the kings of Assyria have destroyed all the nations[NOTE:1] and their lands.
notes: The Hebrew text here has “all the lands,” but the parallel text in 2 Kgs 19:17 has “the nations.”

verses.zh: 将列国的神像都扔在火里；因为他本不是神，乃是人手所造的，是木头、石头的，所以灭绝他。
verses.en: They have burned the gods of the nations,[NOTE:1] for they are not really gods, but only the product of human hands manufactured from wood and stone. That is why the Assyrians could destroy them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and they put their gods in the fire.”
Heb “so they destroyed them” (NASB similar).

verses.zh: 耶和华―我们的　神啊，现在求你救我们脱离亚述王的手，使天下万国都知道惟有你是耶和华。」
verses.en: Now, O Lord our God, rescue us from his power, so all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the Lord.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The parallel text in 2 Kgs 19:19 reads, “that you, Lord, are the only God.”

verses.zh: 亚摩斯的儿子以赛亚就打发人去见希西家，说：「耶和华―以色列的　神如此说，你既然求我攻击亚述王西拿基立，
verses.en: Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: “This is what the Lord God of Israel has said: ‘As to what you have prayed to me concerning King Sennacherib of Assyria,[NOTE:1]
notes: The parallel text in 2 Kgs 19:20 includes a verb, “What you have prayed … I have heard.”

verses.zh: 所以耶和华论他这样说：锡安的处女藐视你，嗤笑你；耶路撒冷的女子向你摇头。
verses.en: this is what the Lord says about him:[NOTE:1] “‘The virgin daughter Zion[NOTE:2] despises you—she makes fun of you;daughter Jerusalem shakes her head after you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “this is the word which the Lord has spoken about him.”

Zion (Jerusalem) is pictured here as a young, vulnerable daughter whose purity is being threatened by the would-be Assyrian rapist. The personification hints at the reality which the young girls of the city would face if the Assyrians conquered it.
Shaking the head was a mocking gesture of derision.

verses.zh: 你辱骂谁，亵渎谁？扬起声来，高举眼目攻击谁呢？乃是攻击以色列的圣者。
verses.en: “‘Whom have you taunted and hurled insults at?At whom have you shoutedand looked so arrogantly?[NOTE:1] At the Holy One of Israel![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and lifted your eyes on high?” Cf. NIV “lifted your eyes in pride”; NRSV “haughtily lifted your eyes.”
See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

verses.zh: 你藉你的臣仆辱骂主说：我率领许多战车上山顶，到黎巴嫩极深之处；我要砍伐其中高大的香柏树和佳美的松树。我必上极高之处，进入肥田的树林。
verses.en: Through your messengers you taunted the Lord,[NOTE:1] “With my many chariots I climbed upthe high mountains,the slopes of Lebanon.I cut down its tall cedarsand its best evergreens.I invaded its remotest regions,[NOTE:2] its thickest woods.
notes: The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
Heb “the height of its extremity”; ASV “its farthest height.”

verses.zh: 我已经挖井喝水；我必用脚掌踏干埃及的一切河。
verses.en: I dug wellsand drank water.[NOTE:1] With the soles of my feet I dried upall the rivers of Egypt.”’
notes: The Hebrew text has simply, “I dug and drank water.” But the parallel text in 2 Kgs 19:24 has “foreign waters.” זָרִים (zarim, “foreign”) may have accidentally dropped out of the Isaianic text by homoioteleuton (cf. NCV, NIV, NLT). Note that the preceding word, מַיִם (mayim, “water) also ends in mem (ם). The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has “foreign waters” for this line. However, in several other passages the 1QIsaa scroll harmonizes with 2 Kgs 19 against the MT (Isa 36:5; 37:9, 20). Since the addition of “foreign” to this text in Isaiah by a later scribe would be more likely than its deletion, the MT reading should be accepted.

verses.zh: 耶和华说：你岂没有听见我早先所做的、古时所立的吗？现在藉你使坚固城荒废，变为乱堆。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] “Certainly you must have heard![NOTE:2] Long ago I worked it out,in ancient times I planned[NOTE:3] it,and now I am bringing it to pass.The plan is this:Fortified cities will crashinto heaps of ruins.[NOTE:4]
notes: Having quoted the Assyrian king’s arrogant words in vv. 23-24, the Lord now speaks to the king.
Heb “Have you not heard?” The rhetorical question expresses the Lord’s amazement that anyone might be ignorant of what he is about to say.
Heb “formed” (so KJV, ASV).

Heb “and it is to cause to crash into heaps of ruins fortified cities.” The subject of the third feminine singular verb תְהִי (tehi) is the implied plan, referred to in the preceding lines with third feminine singular pronominal suffixes.

verses.zh: 所以其中的居民力量甚小，惊惶羞愧。他们像野草，像青菜，如房顶上的草，又如田间未长成的禾稼。
verses.en: Their residents are powerless;[NOTE:1] they are terrified and ashamed.They are as short-lived as plants in the fieldor green vegetation.[NOTE:2] They are as short-lived as grass on the rooftops[NOTE:3] when it is scorched by the east wind.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “short of hand”; KJV, ASV “of small power”; NASB “short of strength.”
Heb “they are plants in the field and green vegetation.” The metaphor emphasizes how short-lived these seemingly powerful cities really were. See Ps 90:5-6; Isa 40:6-8, 24.
Heb “[they are] grass on the rooftops.” See the preceding note.

The Hebrew text has “scorched before the standing grain” (perhaps meaning “before it reaches maturity”), but it is preferable to emend קָמָה (qamah, “standing grain”) to קָדִים (qadim, “east wind”) with the support of 1Q Isaa; cf. J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:657, n. 8.

verses.zh: 你坐下，你出去，你进来，你向我发烈怒，我都知道。
verses.en: I know where you liveand everything you doand how you rage against me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your going out and your coming in and how you have raged against me.” Several scholars have suggested that this line is probably dittographic (note the beginning of the next line). However, most English translations include the statement in question at the end of v. 28 and the beginning of v. 29. Interestingly, the LXX does not have this clause at the end of v. 28 and the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa does not have it at the beginning of v. 29. In light of this ambiguous manuscript evidence, it appears best to retain the clause in both verses.

verses.zh: 因你向我发烈怒，又因你狂傲的话达到我耳中，我就要用钩子钩上你的鼻子，把嚼环放在你口里，使你从原路转回去。
verses.en: Because you rage against meand the uproar you create has reached my ears,[NOTE:1] I will put my hook in your nose,[NOTE:2] and my bit between your lips,and I will lead you back the way you came.
notes: Heb “and your complacency comes up into my ears.” The parallelism is improved if שַׁאֲנַנְךָ (shaʾananekha, “your complacency”) is emended to שְׁאוֹנְךָ (sheʾonekha, “your uproar”). See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 237-38. However, the LXX seems to support the MT, and Sennacherib’s cavalier dismissal of Yahweh depicts an arrogant complacency (J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah [NICOT], 1:658, n. 10).
The word-picture has a parallel in Assyrian sculpture. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 238.

verses.zh: 「以色列人哪，我赐你们一个证据：你们今年要吃自生的，明年也要吃自长的，至于后年，你们要耕种收割，栽植葡萄园，吃其中的果子。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] “This will be your reminder that I have spoken the truth:[NOTE:2] This year you will eat what grows wild,[NOTE:3] and next year[NOTE:4] what grows on its own. But the year after that[NOTE:5] you will plant seed and harvest crops; you will plant vines and consume their produce.[NOTE:6]
notes: At this point the word concerning the king of Assyria (vv. 22-29) ends, and the Lord again addresses Hezekiah and the people directly (see v. 21).

Heb “and this is your sign.” In this case the אוֹת (ʾot, “sign”) is a future reminder of God’s intervention designated before the actual intervention takes place. For similar “signs” see Exod 3:12 and Isa 7:14-25.
This refers to crops that grew up on their own (that is, without cultivation) from the seed planted in past years.
Heb “and in the second year” (so ASV).
Heb “in the third year” (so KJV, NAB).
The four plural imperatival verb forms in v. 30b are used rhetorically. The Lord commands the people to plant, harvest, etc. to emphasize the certainty of restored peace and prosperity.

verses.zh: 犹大家所逃脱余剩的，仍要往下扎根，向上结果。
verses.en: Those who remain in Judah will take root in the ground and bear fruit.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “The remnant of the house of Judah that is left will add roots below and produce fruit above.”

verses.zh: 必有余剩的民从耶路撒冷而出；必有逃脱的人从锡安山而来。万军之耶和华的热心必成就这事。
verses.en: “For a remnant will leave Jerusalem; survivors will come out of Mount Zion.The zeal of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies[NOTE:1] will accomplish this.
notes: Traditionally, “the Lord of hosts.” In this context the Lord’s “zeal” refers to his intense devotion to and love for his people that prompts him to protect and restore them.

verses.zh: 「所以耶和华论亚述王如此说：他必不得来到这城，也不在这里射箭，不得拿盾牌到城前，也不筑垒攻城。
verses.en: “So this is what the Lord says about the king of Assyria: “‘He will not enter this city,nor will he shoot an arrow here.[NOTE:1] He will not attack it with his shielded warriors,[NOTE:2] nor will he build siege works against it.
notes: Heb “there” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV). In terms of English style “here” is expected in collocation with “this” in the previous line.
Heb “[with] a shield” (so ASV, NASB, NRSV).

verses.zh: 他从哪条路来，必从那条路回去，必不得来到这城。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: He will go back the way he came—he will not enter this city,’ says the Lord.

verses.zh: 因我为自己的缘故，又为我仆人大卫的缘故，必保护拯救这城。」
verses.en: I will shield this city and rescue it for the sake of my reputation and because of my promise to David my servant.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for my sake and for the sake of David my servant.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的使者出去，在亚述营中杀了十八万五千人。清早有人起来一看，都是死尸了。
verses.en: The angel of the Lord went out and killed 185,000 troops[NOTE:1] in the Assyrian camp. When they[NOTE:2] got up early the next morning, there were all the corpses![NOTE:3]
notes: The word “troops” is supplied in the translation for smoothness and clarity.
This refers to the Israelites and/or the rest of the Assyrian army.
Heb “look, all of them were dead bodies”; NLT “they found corpses everywhere.”

verses.zh: 亚述王西拿基立就拔营回去，住在尼尼微。
verses.en: So King Sennacherib of Assyria broke camp and went on his way. He went home and stayed in Nineveh.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Sennacherib king of Assyria departed and went and returned and lived in Nineveh.”

verses.zh: 一日在他的神―尼斯洛庙里叩拜，他儿子亚得米勒和沙利色用刀杀了他，就逃到亚拉腊地。他儿子以撒哈顿接续他作王。
verses.en: One day,[NOTE:1] as he was worshiping[NOTE:2] in the temple of his god Nisroch,[NOTE:3] his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword.[NOTE:4] They ran away to the land of Ararat; his son Esarhaddon replaced him as king.
notes: The assassination of King Sennacherib probably took place in 681 b.c.
The verb that introduces this verse serves as a discourse particle and is untranslated; see note on “in the future” in 2:2.

No such Mesopotamian god is presently known. Perhaps the name Nisroch is a textual variation of Nusku, the Mesopotamian god of light and fire. Other proposals have tried to relate the name to Ashur, the chief god of the Assyria, or to Ninurta, the Assyrian god of war.
Extra-biblical sources also mention the assassination of Sennacherib, though they refer to only one assassin. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 239-40.
